facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary reading is that the cash weakness is seasonal and that reported EBITDA understates improvement: adjusted net leverage is 2.98x and the first-quarter outflow had reversed by the third quarter. The view would turn more positive if operating cash flow before receivable sales recovers towards the prior-year level in the fourth quarter, and more negative if the balance of sold receivables stops growing, if federal funding delays push working capital out again, or if the unquantified interest saving from the amendment does not appear in cash interest. Basis: calculation C50; calculation C59; calculation C60; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9, 21

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- No maturity ladder after the 24 April 2026 amendment is printed, so the debt maturities table shows the schedule printed at 3 October 2025, which predates the new Term Loan A, the revised Term Loan B and the larger revolver; this restricts any view of repayments from fiscal 2027 to 2031 to the stated amortisation percentages. Severity Medium; the executed amendment or a lender schedule would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 150; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12 - The fiscal 2024 leverage ratios are not calculable because the 27 September 2024 balance sheet includes the acquired business while fiscal 2024 EBITDA does not, and the annual report gives only unaudited pro forma revenue and net income for that year. Severity Medium; pro forma combined EBITDA would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 117–118, 132 - EBITDA (Reported) is not stated by the issuer for fiscal years, so it is calculated from net income attributable to common shareholders, depreciation, amortization, interest expense and other, net, and income taxes for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025; the interim figures are the issuer's own EBITDA before add-backs. Severity Low; an issuer statement of the figure would close it. Basis: calculation C3; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12 - Several statement lines print a dash or exist in only one filing layout, so they are not supplied for the affected columns: goodwill impairment charges, loss on extinguishment of debt and gain on acquisition of controlling interest in the income statement; amortization of deferred loan costs, derivative instruments, goodwill impairment, gain on acquisition, repayments under other agreements, capital contributions, term loan and senior note proceeds and debt issuance fees in the cash flow statement; and the foreign exchange effect on cash for the nine months to 3 July 2026, where the other lines add to the net change without it. Severity Low; none changes a total. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 114–116; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2–5 - The line for net income attributable to non-controlling interests is printed with positive amounts that add to net income in the annual report and the nine-month statements, and with brackets that subtract in the quarterly releases; it is kept as printed and the attributable total is used. Severity Low. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl, page 8 - Instrument-level carrying values are not disclosed, only principal by instrument and one unamortized discount and cost total of USD 50 million at 3 July 2026; the USD 9 million other debt line has no stated description, rank, rate or maturity and is left out of the debt stack. Severity Low; the debt note detail would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 10 - The covenant level and definition after the 24 April 2026 amendment are not stated: the annual report gives a revolver test of 5.25x first lien net leverage stepping down to 5.00x, while the quarterly reports say only that Term Loan A and the revolver carry a financial covenant under certain circumstances. Severity High for any headroom conclusion; the executed amendment would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 13 - There is no balance sheet at 27 June 2025 in the sources, so net debt and leverage are not supplied for the nine months to 27 June 2025. Severity Low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 4 - The latest balance sheet is dated 3 July 2026 and no fiscal 2026 year-end result is supplied; no subsequent event after 3 July 2026 is stated, so the post-balance-sheet table holds none. Severity Medium; the fourth-quarter release would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 32 - The annual report describes the guarantees of the senior notes due 2032 as senior unsecured yet names the note trustee also as collateral agent, so the notes are ranked second here on the stated guarantee wording and their security is not independently established. Severity Medium; the indenture would close it. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 149 - USD 123 million of the USD 459 million of cash at 3 July 2026 sits in consolidated joint ventures that are variable interest entities, and the filings do not say whether it is free for debt service. Severity Medium. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13 - Receivables sold under the receivable purchase agreement are a non-debt funding source: USD 300 million of receivables stood sold to the purchaser at 3 July 2026 against a USD 400 million maximum (USD 158 million after cash collected but not yet remitted), the net inflow of USD 120 million in the nine months supports operating cash flow, and the agreement term is not printed. Severity Medium; the agreement terms would close it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 9 - Capital expenditure is stated only as purchase of property and equipment, with no maintenance and growth split. Severity Low. Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 4 - Fiscal 2025 has 53 weeks, one more than fiscal 2024 and 2023, and the issuer does not quantify the extra week. Severity Low. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 117–118 - The quarterly reports carry no lease or pension note, so operating lease liabilities of USD 224 million and the defined benefit position are available only at 3 October 2025; they sit outside the debt figure. Severity Low. Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 139–140, 152 - The issuer's net leverage in the releases uses principal debt and last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA, 3.0x at 3 July 2026, and differs from the carrying-value, reported-EBITDA ratios here; both are shown and neither is the covenant measure. Severity Low. Basis: calculation C69; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a Medium rating is that the record is cleaner than that: no dividend, buyback or sponsor fee in fiscal 2025, USD 847 million of voluntary debt reduction, a majority-independent board and a clean audit all point to Low. The rating stays Medium because creditor protection is judged from summaries: the credit agreement, indenture and stockholders agreement are not supplied, the sponsor's holding is unknown, and the restrictions that held back buybacks and large disposals were due to end in September 2026. The view would move to Low if the proxy statement shows the sponsor group below 15% with no further consent rights and the credit agreement shows tight restricted-payment baskets; it would move to High if a dividend, a debt-funded buyback or acquisition, or a non-pro-rata amendment appeared, or if overruns on the fixed-price contracts now gaining share began to erode margins. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The 2024 transaction merged the sponsor-owned legacy Amentum business with the Critical Mission Solutions business and part of the Divergent Solutions business of Jacobs, spun off in a tax-efficient reverse Morris Trust that closed on 27 September 2024. Before the spin-off the acquired business paid about USD 911 million in cash to Jacobs; Jacobs shareholders received 58.5% of the shares, the sponsor-owned equityholder 37.0% and 4.5% sat in escrow until March 2025, when 3.5% went to Jacobs shareholders and 1.0% to the sponsor group. Total consideration was USD 4,032 million, the legacy business was the accounting acquirer and goodwill of USD 3,004 million was recognised, so fiscal 2024 results exclude the acquired business and fiscal 2025 includes it for the full year. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case for a better view is the trend and the issuer's own measure: net leverage fell from 3.53x to 3.32x, the issuer prints 3.0x on principal debt and Adjusted EBITDA, USD 847 million of debt has been repaid voluntarily since June 2025, book-to-bill was 1.1x in the third quarter and 1.3x over the last twelve months, and operating cash flow of USD 225 million and USD 146 million in the second and third quarters reversed the first-quarter outflow. The view would improve if the fourth quarter delivers at least the USD 312 million of free cash flow that the low end of guidance requires without further receivable sales, if funded backlog recovers above its fiscal 2025 year-end level of USD 5,585 million, or if the covenant level and a numeric leverage target are disclosed. It would weaken if fourth-quarter free cash flow falls short of that level, if funded backlog keeps falling, if another funding lapse occurs, if the sponsor group sells down or the board adopts buybacks now that the tax-agreement limits have lapsed, or if fixed-price estimates reverse. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: A funding lapse or continuing resolution like the one that ended on 12 November 2025 is the realistic downside: billing and collections slip, revenue falls, as it did by 2.51% in the nine months to 3 July 2026, and operating cash flow turns negative as in the first quarter, when the outflow was USD 136 million and free cash flow was an outflow of USD 142 million. Working capital then absorbs cash (USD 303 million in nine months), the receivable sale balance has only USD 100 million of headroom under its maximum, and liquidity of USD 1,376 million is 10.12x the first-quarter outflow, so liquidity distress is not the likely outcome. Leverage is the casualty: if reported EBITDA fell USD 100 million the ratio would be 3.69x against 3.32x, and with no dividend to cut, little capital spending to defer and voluntary prepayments as the main lever, recovery to current leverage would take longer rather than fail. Observable signals are funded backlog, the fourth-quarter cash result against USD 312 million, the receivable sold balance and any revolver draw. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Amentum presents an adequate business profile supported by federal backlog, cost-plus contracts and light capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by a thin margin, funded backlog of only 12.94% and cash conversion that leans on receivable sales. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because costs are largely passed through and liquidity is USD 1,376 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the amended facilities holding to 2031 and on leverage staying near 3.32x. The primary downside path is a federal funding lapse that delays billing and cash while fixed-price estimates weaken. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the proxy statement, peer and rating evidence, and the fourth-quarter result. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: federal funding timing hitting cash conversion. Basis: calculation C75; calculation C10; calculation C3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The sources support a credit snapshot of Amentum Holdings, Inc. with limits: figures are usable to 3 July 2026, but covenant headroom after the April 2026 credit agreement amendment, governance detail and any later event cannot be confirmed.

Fiscal 2025 includes the merged Critical Mission Solutions business for the full year while fiscal 2024 does not, and fiscal 2025 has 53 weeks, so growth and margin trends across the two years are not like for like. The run settings call the second quarter current, but the newest filing covers the third quarter ended 3 July 2026, so each figure must carry the period its filing states.

## Gaps

- The run settings name the second quarter of 2026 as the current period and fiscal 2025 as the prior period, but the newest filing covers the third quarter ended 3 July 2026. This module has changed neither label; each later module should state the period its filing gives, and the user should confirm which quarter is intended.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 1–3

- The fiscal 2024 and 2023 statements of operations and cash flows exclude the Critical Mission Solutions business acquired on 27 September 2024, fiscal 2025 runs 53 weeks, and the only combined view is unaudited pro forma revenue and net income for fiscal 2024 and 2023. Growth, margin, leverage and coverage comparisons across those years are therefore not like for like.

- The credit agreement, the indenture and the April 2026 first amendment are listed as exhibits but are not supplied. The annual report gives a Revolver test of 5.25x first lien net leverage stepping down to 5.00x, but the quarterly filings say only that Term Loan A and the Revolver carry a financial covenant under certain circumstances, so the level, definition and headroom after the amendment are not established.

- Directors, executive pay, beneficial ownership and related-party information are incorporated by reference to the 2026 proxy statement, which is not supplied, so Business & governance rests on the annual report's risk factors, its summary of the stockholders agreement and its signature page.

- No rating-agency document is supplied and the run settings list no ratings. The only mention is a headline in the 9 February 2026 release, “Moody's Upgraded Credit Rating to Ba3, from Ba1”; on the agency's long-term scale (general knowledge, not a supplied source) Ba1 ranks above Ba3, so the headline contradicts itself and neither the direction nor the current rating is established.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-09_exhibit991-february92026.htm.jsonl, page 1

- The annual report describes the guarantees of the senior notes due 2032 as senior unsecured yet names the note trustee also as collateral agent, and the indenture is not supplied, so whether the notes carry collateral is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 149

- The latest balance sheet is dated 3 July 2026, 125 days before the as-of date, and no filing after 11 August 2026 is supplied. The fiscal year ends on the Friday nearest the end of September, so fiscal 2026 should have ended around 2 October 2026 (an inference, not stated); its results are not available, and nothing between August and November 2026 is evidenced.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 117–118; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 32; calculation C12
- New term loans of USD 2,991 million at the amendment exceeded the USD 2,981 million Term Loan outstanding at 3 April 2026 by USD 10 million, and the supplied text does not say why.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-04-03_amtm-20260403.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 11

- Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow and net leverage are management definitions. Net leverage is stated only in the three releases (3.4x at 2 January 2026, 3.2x at 3 April 2026 and 3.0x at 3 July 2026) and in no filing, and the wording of the discrete items differs among the annual report, the quarterly reports and the releases.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-09_exhibit991-february92026.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 102; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16

- Consolidated joint ventures that are variable interest entities hold USD 123 million of the USD 459 million of cash at 3 July 2026, and the filings do not say whether that cash is free for debt service.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13

- The run settings carry no market quotes, peer set, portfolio or fund limits, and no research question was supplied, so market-implied, peer and portfolio work cannot be supported from these sources.

spans.text: # CP-1 Financial foundation for Amentum Holdings, Inc. (amtm)
## Request

Amentum Holdings, Inc. (issuer id amtm), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity, coverage and reported-basis credit metrics from the seven supplied filings and releases, in USD millions, to the third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-03.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Amentum Holdings, Inc. for the fiscal year ended October 3, 2025 (53 weeks), with the auditor's report | 2025-11-25 | 8273d25a00529c2b44154e4079fb17aed384ffabfb0b6e916ff874e87d184e2c | Audited FY2023 to FY2025 statements, debt note, segment Adjusted EBITDA, receivable sales, leases and pensions |

| EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, quarter ended April 3, 2026 | 2026-05-11 | 70874f67722755b78375d913af6706b9925581a1e0d597e3dc867f0ae2da1e41 | Quarter and six-month EBITDA reconciliation, last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA and net leverage at 2026-04-03 |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | Earlier module output supplied by CP-OS: source readiness for this run | not stated | 95a8497735ccb0e6eef9c6a563094da6ff5999ab9dc4e50ba0232d99b76e210d | Source dates, perimeter limits and gaps carried forward |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is falling, but cash generation is weaker than earnings suggest: net debt was 3.32x LTM reported EBITDA at 3 July 2026 against 3.53x at fiscal 2025 year-end, and nine-month operating cash flow of USD 235 million includes USD 120 million of receivable sales.
Basis: calculation C47; calculation C29; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9

Interest is covered 3.53x by reported EBITDA and no named facility or note matures before 2031, so the near-term risk is cash conversion rather than refinancing. Comparisons with fiscal 2024 are not like for like because that year excludes the acquired business, so trends start at fiscal 2025.
Basis: calculation C48; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 118
### Key findings

Net debt fell from USD 3,506 million at fiscal 2025 year-end to USD 3,366 million at 3 July 2026 while LTM reported EBITDA rose from USD 994 million to USD 1,013 million, so net leverage eased from 3.53x to 3.32x and total debt leverage from 3.97x to 3.78x. The USD 125 million voluntary payment on Term Loan B on 30 June 2026 cut debt and cash together, so it left net debt unchanged.
Basis: calculation C19; calculation C25; calculation C8; calculation C46; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 12

Cash interest paid fell from USD 306 million in fiscal 2025 to USD 287 million on an LTM basis at 3 July 2026, lifting reported EBITDA cover from 3.25x to 3.53x. The April 2026 amendment lowered the Term Loan B margin from 2.25% to 1.75% over Term SOFR, but the filings do not quantify the saving.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C48; calculation C85; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 116, 147; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 12

Operating cash flow for the nine months to 3 July 2026 was USD 235 million against USD 273 million a year earlier, and a higher balance of receivables sold under the receivable purchase agreement supplied USD 120 million of it against USD 42 million a year earlier, so operating cash flow before receivable sales was USD 115 million against USD 231 million. Working capital absorbed USD 303 million, chiefly accrued compensation (USD 160 million) and payables (USD 198 million); the first-quarter operating outflow of USD 136 million reversed in the second and third quarters, which fits timing rather than erosion but cannot be proved from the filings.
Basis: calculation C59; calculation C60; calculation C61; calculation C97; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9

Capital expenditure is light at USD 27 million in fiscal 2025, 0.19% of revenue, so operating cash flow less capital expenditure of USD 516 million tracks operating cash flow; the issuer's own free cash flow excludes contributions to equity method investments, which were USD 56 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 53 million in the nine months to 3 July 2026.
Basis: calculation C63; calculation C62; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 5

Cash of USD 459 million and revolver availability of USD 917 million give liquidity of USD 1,376 million at 3 July 2026, although USD 123 million of the cash sits in consolidated joint ventures that the filings do not say is freely available. After the April 2026 amendment the revolver and Term Loan A mature on 24 April 2031, Term Loan B on 27 September 2031 and the senior notes on 1 August 2032, so scheduled amortisation is the only near-term repayment among the named instruments, apart from USD 9 million of other debt whose maturity is not stated.
Basis: calculation C52; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10–13

Reported EBITDA is calculated from the issuer's own reconciliation lines because the annual report states only Adjusted EBITDA. The issuer's adjusted measure adds USD 110 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 76 million in the nine months to 3 July 2026, mainly acquisition costs and share-based compensation, and on the same carrying-value debt it would put net leverage at 2.98x.
Basis: calculation C64; calculation C65; calculation C50; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 157; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary reading is that the cash weakness is seasonal and that reported EBITDA understates improvement: adjusted net leverage is 2.98x and the first-quarter outflow had reversed by the third quarter. The view would turn more positive if operating cash flow before receivable sales recovers towards the prior-year level in the fourth quarter, and more negative if the balance of sold receivables stops growing, if federal funding delays push working capital out again, or if the unquantified interest saving from the amendment does not appear in cash interest.
Basis: calculation C50; calculation C59; calculation C60; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 9, 21

## Gaps

- No maturity ladder after the 24 April 2026 amendment is printed, so the debt maturities table shows the schedule printed at 3 October 2025, which predates the new Term Loan A, the revised Term Loan B and the larger revolver; this restricts any view of repayments from fiscal 2027 to 2031 to the stated amortisation percentages. Severity Medium; the executed amendment or a lender schedule would close it.

- The fiscal 2024 leverage ratios are not calculable because the 27 September 2024 balance sheet includes the acquired business while fiscal 2024 EBITDA does not, and the annual report gives only unaudited pro forma revenue and net income for that year. Severity Medium; pro forma combined EBITDA would close it.

- EBITDA (Reported) is not stated by the issuer for fiscal years, so it is calculated from net income attributable to common shareholders, depreciation, amortization, interest expense and other, net, and income taxes for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025; the interim figures are the issuer's own EBITDA before add-backs. Severity Low; an issuer statement of the figure would close it.
Basis: calculation C3; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12

- Several statement lines print a dash or exist in only one filing layout, so they are not supplied for the affected columns: goodwill impairment charges, loss on extinguishment of debt and gain on acquisition of controlling interest in the income statement; amortization of deferred loan costs, derivative instruments, goodwill impairment, gain on acquisition, repayments under other agreements, capital contributions, term loan and senior note proceeds and debt issuance fees in the cash flow statement; and the foreign exchange effect on cash for the nine months to 3 July 2026, where the other lines add to the net change without it. Severity Low; none changes a total.

- The line for net income attributable to non-controlling interests is printed with positive amounts that add to net income in the annual report and the nine-month statements, and with brackets that subtract in the quarterly releases; it is kept as printed and the attributable total is used. Severity Low.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl, page 8

- Instrument-level carrying values are not disclosed, only principal by instrument and one unamortized discount and cost total of USD 50 million at 3 July 2026; the USD 9 million other debt line has no stated description, rank, rate or maturity and is left out of the debt stack. Severity Low; the debt note detail would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 10

- The covenant level and definition after the 24 April 2026 amendment are not stated: the annual report gives a revolver test of 5.25x first lien net leverage stepping down to 5.00x, while the quarterly reports say only that Term Loan A and the revolver carry a financial covenant under certain circumstances. Severity High for any headroom conclusion; the executed amendment would close it.
- There is no balance sheet at 27 June 2025 in the sources, so net debt and leverage are not supplied for the nine months to 27 June 2025. Severity Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 4

- The latest balance sheet is dated 3 July 2026 and no fiscal 2026 year-end result is supplied; no subsequent event after 3 July 2026 is stated, so the post-balance-sheet table holds none. Severity Medium; the fourth-quarter release would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 32

- The annual report describes the guarantees of the senior notes due 2032 as senior unsecured yet names the note trustee also as collateral agent, so the notes are ranked second here on the stated guarantee wording and their security is not independently established. Severity Medium; the indenture would close it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 149

- USD 123 million of the USD 459 million of cash at 3 July 2026 sits in consolidated joint ventures that are variable interest entities, and the filings do not say whether it is free for debt service. Severity Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13

- Receivables sold under the receivable purchase agreement are a non-debt funding source: USD 300 million of receivables stood sold to the purchaser at 3 July 2026 against a USD 400 million maximum (USD 158 million after cash collected but not yet remitted), the net inflow of USD 120 million in the nine months supports operating cash flow, and the agreement term is not printed. Severity Medium; the agreement terms would close it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 9
- Capital expenditure is stated only as purchase of property and equipment, with no maintenance and growth split. Severity Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 4
- Fiscal 2025 has 53 weeks, one more than fiscal 2024 and 2023, and the issuer does not quantify the extra week. Severity Low.

- The quarterly reports carry no lease or pension note, so operating lease liabilities of USD 224 million and the defined benefit position are available only at 3 October 2025; they sit outside the debt figure. Severity Low.

- The issuer's net leverage in the releases uses principal debt and last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA, 3.0x at 3 July 2026, and differs from the carrying-value, reported-EBITDA ratios here; both are shown and neither is the covenant measure. Severity Low.
Basis: calculation C69; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance for Amentum Holdings, Inc. (amtm)
## Request

Amentum Holdings, Inc. (issuer id amtm), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, transactions, ownership, governance and sponsor behaviour that the seven supplied filings and releases state, to the third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-03.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors face concentrated federal demand and thin margins rather than sponsor extraction: no distribution or creditor-adverse action is documented, but the restrictions on buybacks and asset sales were due to lapse in September 2026 and the sponsor group's current stake is not disclosed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; calculation C56

Sponsor and governance risk is Medium on incomplete evidence, not on conduct. Federal agencies supplied 81.09% of fiscal 2025 revenue, adjusted EBITDA margin was 7.67%, and only 12.94% of the USD 48,237 million backlog is funded.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C18; calculation C45; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 28
### Key findings

The customer base is deep but concentrated: federal agencies supplied 81.09% of fiscal 2025 revenue (USD 11,672 million of USD 14,393 million), led by the Department of War and the intelligence community at 53.35%, while commercial and international customers rose to 18.91% from 9.55% after the merger. Federal contracts can be terminated for the government's convenience or curtailed at little notice, and the shutdown that ended on 12 November 2025 reduced nine-month revenue, so concentration shows up first as funding-timing risk and only later as customer loss.

Basis: calculation C2; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 25

Backlog gives multi-year visibility but little funded certainty: total backlog of USD 48,237 million at 3 July 2026 equals 3.41 years of last twelve months revenue, yet only USD 6,240 million (12.94%) is funded, about 5.30 months of revenue. Funded backlog fell by 26.16% during fiscal 2025 while total backlog rose by 4.83%, so conversion to cash depends on annual appropriations rather than on the size of the book.
Basis: calculation C44; calculation C45; calculation C46; calculation C48; calculation C49; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28

Margin improvement is real but partly a shift to riskier contract types: the nine-month adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 8.11% from 7.68%, yet cost-plus-fee work fell from 64.15% to 55.88% of revenue while fixed-price work rose from 23.45% to 29.54%, and net favourable cumulative catch-up adjustments equal 10.02% of nine-month adjusted EBITDA against 4.98% a year earlier. The auditor's one critical audit matter concerns revenue recognition on certain fixed-price contracts, so the contract type gaining share is also the one that depends most on management estimates.

Basis: calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C50; calculation C51; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 113

Ownership is dispersed but sponsor-influenced, and the sponsor's current stake is unknown: by calculation from merger-date percentages, Jacobs shareholders held 62.0% and the sponsor group 38.0% of the shares after the March 2025 escrow release, the sponsor group can nominate up to five of the 13 directors while it holds 25.1% or more, and most directors are independent. Because the proxy statement that would report current holdings is not supplied, creditors cannot size the sponsor's voting weight or the scale of a possible sell-down.

Basis: calculation C52; calculation C53; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 71; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 164–165

Documented sponsor behaviour is creditor-aligned or neutral: the sponsor group put USD 235 million of cash into the company before the merger, advisory fees of USD 4 million a year were not charged in fiscal 2025, no dividend or buyback is recorded, and voluntary term loan payments since June 2025 total USD 847 million (USD 722 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 125 million on 30 June 2026). The one adverse-leaning feature is a charter provision under which sponsor affiliates owe the company no duty to offer corporate opportunities.

Basis: calculation C59; calculation C60; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 153; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 12

The main change for creditors is flexibility rather than conduct: for two years after the 27 September 2024 closing the tax matters agreement restricted buybacks, sales of 30% or more of the acquired assets and equity transactions that could change control, and the sponsor group was bound to vote for the Executive Chair; both periods ended on 27 September 2026 by calculation, 39 days before the as-of date. The annual report states a policy to retain earnings and repay debt, but the 2026 reports do not restate it and management refers to a target leverage profile that it does not quantify.

Basis: calculation C56; calculation C58; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 69; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 93; EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl, page 3

Joint ventures move reported revenue more than they move earnings: about 30 equity-method ventures contributed equity earnings equal to 12.92% of fiscal 2025 operating income and 15.84% in the nine months to 3 July 2026, related-party revenue from them is only 1.92% of revenue, yet many ventures hold a single contract and the maximum loss exposure is USD 204 million. Contract transitions to joint ventures and fiscal 2025 divestitures together lowered third-quarter revenue by about 3% while equity earnings rose.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a Medium rating is that the record is cleaner than that: no dividend, buyback or sponsor fee in fiscal 2025, USD 847 million of voluntary debt reduction, a majority-independent board and a clean audit all point to Low. The rating stays Medium because creditor protection is judged from summaries: the credit agreement, indenture and stockholders agreement are not supplied, the sponsor's holding is unknown, and the restrictions that held back buybacks and large disposals were due to end in September 2026. The view would move to Low if the proxy statement shows the sponsor group below 15% with no further consent rights and the credit agreement shows tight restricted-payment baskets; it would move to High if a dividend, a debt-funded buyback or acquisition, or a non-pro-rata amendment appeared, or if overruns on the fixed-price contracts now gaining share began to erode margins.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The 2024 transaction merged the sponsor-owned legacy Amentum business with the Critical Mission Solutions business and part of the Divergent Solutions business of Jacobs, spun off in a tax-efficient reverse Morris Trust that closed on 27 September 2024. Before the spin-off the acquired business paid about USD 911 million in cash to Jacobs; Jacobs shareholders received 58.5% of the shares, the sponsor-owned equityholder 37.0% and 4.5% sat in escrow until March 2025, when 3.5% went to Jacobs shareholders and 1.0% to the sponsor group. Total consideration was USD 4,032 million, the legacy business was the accounting acquirer and goodwill of USD 3,004 million was recognised, so fiscal 2024 results exclude the acquired business and fiscal 2025 includes it for the full year.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 128–131; calculation C62; calculation C52; calculation C53

Debt raised at closing was a USD 3,750 million seven-year term facility and a USD 850 million revolver, which replaced the earlier first and second lien agreements, together with USD 1,000 million of senior notes due 2032 sold in August 2024 into escrow. On 24 April 2026 an amendment replaced the term facility with a USD 1,400 million Term Loan A and a USD 1,591 million Term Loan B (USD 1,466 million after a voluntary payment of USD 125 million on 30 June 2026) and raised the revolver to USD 1,000 million; the revolver and Term Loan A mature on 24 April 2031, Term Loan B on 27 September 2031 and the notes on 1 August 2032. Voluntary term loan payments since June 2025 total USD 847 million, and the executed amendment is not supplied, so these terms rest on the filings' summaries.

Other transactions are small by comparison: the sale of the Rapid Solutions hardware business to Lockheed Martin for USD 360 million in cash on 26 June 2025, an undated sale of a New Zealand facilities maintenance business, and a USD 70 million working capital payment in the third quarter of fiscal 2025 that settled the merger price. No acquisition was paid for in the nine months to 3 July 2026, and the receivable purchase agreement maximum was raised to USD 400 million in December 2024 and amended again in March 2026.

## Gaps

- The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so the sponsor group's current holding, other holders above 5%, directors' beneficial ownership, committee membership, executive pay and the related-party policy are not established. Severity High for the governance rating; the proxy statement would close it.

- The credit agreement, indenture, 2026 amendment, stockholders agreement, tax matters agreement and registration rights agreement are exhibits incorporated by reference and are not supplied, so restricted-payment, investment, lien and priming capacity, consent rights and the change-of-control definition are not established. Severity High for any legal-capacity conclusion.

- Sponsor fund vintage, fund life remaining, entry equity value and sell-down intentions are not stated, so exit pressure is not inferred; the only sponsor money documented is the USD 235 million cash contribution before the merger. Severity Medium.
- Customer concentration is stated by customer type only; no contract or programme share is given, so reliance on a few large programmes is not established. Severity Medium.

- The annual report dated 25 November 2025 states a policy to retain earnings and repay debt; the 2026 reports do not restate it, and the tax matters limits ended on 2026-09-27 by calculation, so the board's current intention on dividends and buybacks is not established. Severity Medium; the fiscal 2026 annual report would close it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 93–94; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66; calculation C56
- The May 2026 release refers to a target leverage profile and gives no figure, so how far debt reduction is meant to go is not established. Severity Medium.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl, page 3

- The acquired business is excluded from fiscal 2024 operations and the annual report gives no pro forma Adjusted EBITDA, so segment and margin trends across fiscal 2024 and 2025 are not like for like; trends start at fiscal 2025. Severity Medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 132; calculation C26

- The date and price of the New Zealand facilities maintenance sale, the date of the joint venture stake sale beyond the quarter, and the use of the Rapid Solutions proceeds are not stated. Severity Low.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-09_exhibit991-february92026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 105

- Terms of the receivable purchase agreement, including its term and termination triggers, are not supplied although USD 300 million of receivables stood sold at 3 July 2026 against a USD 400 million maximum. Severity Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 9

- The first-quarter release headline says Moody's upgraded the credit rating to Ba3 from Ba1, which contradicts itself, and no rating document is supplied, so no rating is relied on here. Severity Low for this analysis.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-02-09_exhibit991-february92026.htm.jsonl, page 1

- The annual report describes seasonality in words, with federal fiscal-year-end awards that may favour the fiscal fourth quarter and weaker summer and holiday periods, but gives no figures, so quarterly comparisons cannot be adjusted for it. Severity Low.

- No document is dated after 11 August 2026, so any fourth-quarter result, event or ownership change after the third quarter is not established. Severity Medium; the fourth-quarter report would close it.

## Request

Amentum Holdings, Inc. (issuer id amtm), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit profile from the seven supplied filings and releases and the three earlier module outputs, to the third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-03.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Amentum's credit profile is adequate: federal backlog, cost-plus contracts and no named maturity before 2031 support debt service, but 3.32x net leverage, a thin margin and cash conversion helped by receivable sales leave little room for a funding or execution slip.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C81; calculation C74; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12

The primary downside is a repeat of the first-quarter cash squeeze, when operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 136 million, and the full-year free cash flow guidance now needs USD 312 million to USD 362 million in the fourth quarter against USD 261 million a year earlier.
Basis: calculation C90; calculation C39; calculation C40; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Key findings

1. Scale and visibility support debt service, but visibility is thinner than the backlog suggests: USD 48,237 million of backlog equals 3.41 years of last twelve months revenue and federal customers supplied 81.09% of fiscal 2025 revenue, yet only 12.94% of the backlog is funded and nine-month revenue fell 2.51%, so near-term revenue rests on annual appropriations.

Basis: calculation C105; calculation C74; calculation C69; calculation C75; calculation C83; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28

2. Leverage is moderate and falling but not low: net debt of USD 3,366 million is 3.32x last twelve months reported EBITDA against 3.53x at fiscal 2025 year-end and 2.98x on Adjusted EBITDA, and cash interest is covered 3.53x; if reported EBITDA were USD 100 million lower the ratio would be 3.69x.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C6; calculation C59; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, page 10

3. Refinancing is a distant risk and liquidity is ample: no named maturity falls before 24 April 2031, scheduled amortisation is USD 50.91 million over four quarters (10.74% of last twelve months free cash flow), and cash plus revolver availability of USD 1,376 million is 4.54x the nine-month working capital absorption.
Basis: calculation C61; calculation C62; calculation C10; calculation C91; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 12

4. Cash conversion is the weak link: last twelve months free cash flow of USD 474 million is 42.02% of Adjusted EBITDA and 34.84% before USD 81 million of receivable sales, and nine-month free cash flow fell 16.47% to USD 213 million as working capital took USD 303 million, with cash earnings up USD 129 million and operating assets and liabilities using USD 167 million.

Basis: calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C15; calculation C27; calculation C25; calculation C24; calculation C21; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 30

5. The full-year cash guidance is back-end loaded: free cash flow guidance of USD 525 million to USD 575 million implies USD 312 million to USD 362 million in the fourth quarter, which is 19.54% to 38.70% above the USD 261 million of a year earlier and 108.71% to 116.03% of implied Adjusted EBITDA against 87.00%, so a collection delay or a repeat funding lapse would show first as a guidance miss.
Basis: calculation C39; calculation C40; calculation C41; calculation C42; calculation C36; calculation C37; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, page 4

6. The margin gain comes from overhead, not from contract profit: Adjusted EBITDA rose USD 24 million in the nine months because other segment expenses fell USD 89 million, while revenue less cost of revenues fell USD 65 million even though net favourable estimate adjustments were USD 43 million higher; at a 7.67% margin, one percentage point on last twelve months revenue is USD 141.3 million, or 12.53% of last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA.
Basis: calculation C52; calculation C51; calculation C49; calculation C53; calculation C81; calculation C58; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 16

7. Contract mix is shifting toward fixed-price work: cost-plus-fee work fell from 64.15% to 55.88% of nine-month revenue and fixed-price work rose from 23.45% to 29.54%, which adds margin upside and estimate risk together, and the auditor's one critical audit matter concerns this contract type.
Basis: calculation C78; calculation C79; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 113

8. Financial policy is creditor-friendly today but less constrained from September 2026: USD 847 million of voluntary debt reduction since June 2025 and no dividend or buyback are documented, yet the tax-agreement limits on buybacks and large disposals were due to end on 27 September 2026, the sponsor group held 38.0% by calculation, and its current stake is not disclosed.
Basis: calculation C89; calculation C87; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, pages 64–66

9. Interest-rate exposure steps up in early 2027: 73.96% of debt is floating, interest rate swaps with a notional of USD 1,300 million cover 45.36% of the floating term debt and mature 87 days after the as-of date, and the issuer puts each 1% rate move at about USD 23 million of nine-month interest expense.
Basis: calculation C64; calculation C65; calculation C66; calculation C101; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case for a better view is the trend and the issuer's own measure: net leverage fell from 3.53x to 3.32x, the issuer prints 3.0x on principal debt and Adjusted EBITDA, USD 847 million of debt has been repaid voluntarily since June 2025, book-to-bill was 1.1x in the third quarter and 1.3x over the last twelve months, and operating cash flow of USD 225 million and USD 146 million in the second and third quarters reversed the first-quarter outflow. The view would improve if the fourth quarter delivers at least the USD 312 million of free cash flow that the low end of guidance requires without further receivable sales, if funded backlog recovers above its fiscal 2025 year-end level of USD 5,585 million, or if the covenant level and a numeric leverage target are disclosed. It would weaken if fourth-quarter free cash flow falls short of that level, if funded backlog keeps falling, if another funding lapse occurs, if the sponsor group sells down or the board adopts buybacks now that the tax-agreement limits have lapsed, or if fixed-price estimates reverse.

### Business and ownership

Amentum is a federal services contractor with two segments, Digital Solutions and Global Engineering Solutions, formed by the September 2024 merger with the Jacobs business, which lifted fiscal 2025 revenue by 71.59% and makes fiscal 2025 the first comparable year. Control is shared: Jacobs shareholders and a sponsor group holding 38.0% by calculation own the shares, no single holder is shown to control the board, and the credit consequence is that a sponsor sell-down, not a sponsor demand, is the ownership event to watch.

### Revenue durability

Revenue is predictable but not growing: federal customers supplied 81.09% of fiscal 2025 revenue under contracts that can be terminated for convenience, remaining performance obligations due within 12 months cover 49.76% of last twelve months revenue, and the book-to-bill of 1.1x in the third quarter and 1.3x over the last twelve months keeps adding backlog. Nine-month revenue fell 2.51% and the guided midpoint is 3.60% below fiscal 2025, so durability rests on awards replacing the revenue lost to joint venture transitions and divestitures, and the August cut to revenue guidance suggests that replacement is slower than planned.

### Margin resilience

Margins are defended by cost pass-through but not widened by it: cost of revenues is 89.90% of revenue, cost-plus-fee work is 55.88% of revenue, and selling, general and administrative expenses fell 17.95% on merger synergies, which is why the nine-month margin rose to 8.11% from 7.68% while revenue less cost of revenues slipped. Synergy savings do not repeat, so further margin gain has to come from awards and execution, and the fixed-price share raises the chance of reversals.

### Competitive forces

Rivals, one buyer class and labour set the margin: the annual report names nine primary competitors and says awards are competed and may favour price, and protests held up two awards until the third quarter, so rivalry caps pricing; entry is limited by security-cleared staff, past performance and the need for teaming and contract vehicles; government insourcing is the substitute risk; buyer power is high because federal customers supplied 81.09% of revenue, may terminate for convenience, and 9.01% of revenue came through other prime contractors; and supplier power sits in labour, materials and subcontractors inside cost of revenues of 89.90% of revenue, which cost-plus pass-through limits. The credit consequence is a stable but price-disciplined margin near 7.67%.

Federal budget timing is a material credit driver: the 2026 budget request lifted defense spending to USD 1.01 trillion, a rise of 13% on the 2025 enacted level, while cutting non-defense discretionary spending by about 21%, and the shutdown that ended on 12 November 2025 cost revenue and delayed cash. ### Outlook

The next 12 to 24 months depend on the fourth quarter and the next appropriation: the August update cut revenue guidance by USD 150 million at the low end and USD 350 million at the high end while raising the low end of Adjusted EBITDA guidance by USD 15 million, applying the issuer's May adjustment to fiscal 2025, the new midpoint implies underlying revenue growth of only 0.96% against about 3% stated in May, and Adjusted EBITDA growth of 5.18%. Fiscal 2025 had 14 weeks in its fourth quarter, so implied revenue per week in the fourth quarter ranges from a decline of 1.36% to an increase of 2.75% against that base if the 2026 quarter has 13 weeks. Over three to five years, nuclear and space awards and a book-to-bill of 1.3x over the last twelve months support growth, while federal budget risk stays the main headwind.

### Downside scenario

A funding lapse or continuing resolution like the one that ended on 12 November 2025 is the realistic downside: billing and collections slip, revenue falls, as it did by 2.51% in the nine months to 3 July 2026, and operating cash flow turns negative as in the first quarter, when the outflow was USD 136 million and free cash flow was an outflow of USD 142 million. Working capital then absorbs cash (USD 303 million in nine months), the receivable sale balance has only USD 100 million of headroom under its maximum, and liquidity of USD 1,376 million is 10.12x the first-quarter outflow, so liquidity distress is not the likely outcome. Leverage is the casualty: if reported EBITDA fell USD 100 million the ratio would be 3.69x against 3.32x, and with no dividend to cut, little capital spending to defer and voluntary prepayments as the main lever, recovery to current leverage would take longer rather than fail. Observable signals are funded backlog, the fourth-quarter cash result against USD 312 million, the receivable sold balance and any revolver draw.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Amentum presents an adequate business profile supported by federal backlog, cost-plus contracts and light capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by a thin margin, funded backlog of only 12.94% and cash conversion that leans on receivable sales. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because costs are largely passed through and liquidity is USD 1,376 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the amended facilities holding to 2031 and on leverage staying near 3.32x. The primary downside path is a federal funding lapse that delays billing and cash while fixed-price estimates weaken. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the proxy statement, peer and rating evidence, and the fourth-quarter result. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: federal funding timing hitting cash conversion.

## Gaps

- The executed credit agreement, the 2026 amendment and the indenture are not supplied, and the quarterly reports say only that a financial covenant applies under certain circumstances, so covenant level, headroom and capacity to distribute cash are not established. Severity High for any covenant or distribution conclusion.

- No peer set, rating document or market price is supplied, so the business profile cannot be compared with typical leveraged issuers in the sector and market-implied risk is not assessed. Severity Medium.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); EX-99.1_2026-02-09_exhibit991-february92026.htm.jsonl, page 1

- The fiscal 2026 year-end date, the weeks in the fourth quarter and whether guidance assumes further receivable sales are not stated, and no fourth-quarter result is supplied, so the fourth-quarter test of guidance is indicative. Severity Medium; the fiscal 2026 annual report would close it.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C33

- The interest saving from the April 2026 repricing is not quantified, and last twelve months cash interest still includes months before the amendment, so forward cover is not established. Severity Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C5
- Management's target leverage profile has no figure, so how far debt reduction is meant to go is not established. Severity Medium.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl, page 3
- No contract-level revenue, recompete schedule or largest-programme share is given, so reliance on a few large programmes is not established beyond the federal share. Severity Medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-10-03_amtm-20251003.htm.jsonl, page 133
- Hedging after the swaps mature on 31 January 2027 is not stated, so interest cost beyond that date is not established. Severity Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C66

- The gross favourable and unfavourable estimate adjustments are printed (USD 203 million and USD 120 million in nine months) but the programmes behind them are not, so the quality of the margin gain is judged from totals. Severity Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 8

- USD 123 million of cash sits in consolidated joint ventures and the filings do not say whether it is free for debt service, so liquidity excluding it is shown alongside the headline figure. Severity Low.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C11

- The issuer's own adjustment of USD 650 million to fiscal 2025 revenue for working days, divestitures and joint venture transitions is stated in the May release and not restated in August, so underlying growth after the August cut is worked on the May adjustment. Severity Low.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-11_exhibit991-may112026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-08-10_exhibit991-august102026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C98
- No document is dated after 11 August 2026, so any fourth-quarter result, funding lapse or ownership change after the third quarter is not established. Severity Medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-07-03_amtm-20260703.htm.jsonl, page 32
